 Rainy Season Arrives, Doctors Warn Parents to Watch Out for ISPA to DBD in Children 
 31 Oktober 2026, 11:24 | Editorial Team 
 Didi Kurniawan 
 Reporter 
 Didi Kurniawan 
 Editor 
 Illustration. (Photo: Unsplash) 
 Share:
 JAKARTA - The Children's Specialist Doctor of the Sebelas Maret State University Hospital (UNS) Solo, dr. Aisya Fikritama Aditya, Sp.A, reminded parents to pay more attention to children's health during the transition from the dry season to the rainy season.
 According to Aisya, weather changes do not directly cause children to get sick. However, changes in temperature and humidity, activity patterns, and increased exposure to germs in certain environments can affect the risk of infection.
 "This does not mean that weather changes directly make children sick, but changes in temperature and humidity, activity patterns, and increased exposure to germs in certain environments can affect the risk of infection," said Aisya, quoted by Antara, Saturday, October 31.
 He explained that the transition from a prolonged dry season to a rainy season can increase the risk of a number of diseases in children. One of them is acute respiratory tract infections (ARI), such as cough, cold, and influenza.
 In addition, children are also at risk of diarrhea due to the consumption of contaminated food or water. Another disease to watch out for is dengue fever (DBD), especially when there are many puddles of water that are breeding grounds for mosquitoes.
 "If there is a flood, we also need to be aware of leptospirosis, especially in children who come into contact with water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals," said Aisya.
 Aisya said that some of the early symptoms of the disease that parents need to pay attention to include fever, colds, coughs, sore throats, vomiting, diarrhea, and changes in children's behavior that look more tired and less active than usual.
 However, these symptoms do not always indicate the same disease. He reminded parents not to immediately consider fever in the rainy season as a symptom of flu, because the condition can also be caused by DBD or other infections.
 Furthermore, Aisya appealed to parents to immediately take their children to health services if there are signs of danger, such as shortness of breath, loss of consciousness, seizures, or symptoms of dehydration.
 Parents also need to seek medical help immediately if fever is accompanied by severe abdominal pain, constant vomiting, and bleeding.
 Even though the season keeps changing, Aisya emphasizes that maintaining children's health must remain a priority. Parents need to recognize the early symptoms of the disease and not delay the examination if the child shows signs of danger.
 "Recognize the early symptoms of the disease and do not delay the examination if the child shows signs of danger. Because maintaining children's health is not only about treating when they are sick, but also building healthy habits every day," said Aisya, who is also a lecturer at the Faculty of Medicine, UNS.
 Meanwhile, the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) predicts that the 2026/2027 rainy season will begin in November and reach its peak in December 2026.
 BMKG estimates that the early rainy season in November 2026 occurred in 185 Seasonal Zones (ZOM), or covering 24.66 percent of Indonesia's land area. Furthermore, in December 2026, the rainy season is expected to begin in 266 ZOM or about 17.31 percent of the land area.
 BMKG also predicts that the beginning of the 2026/2027 rainy season in most parts of Indonesia has regressed compared to the average climatologist. This condition is influenced by the El Niño phenomenon of category 3.
